title: Adding Lucene-style ?q= query string search for alerts made the Postgres backend build WHERE clauses by str.format()-ing user search terms into SQL.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: User-controlled input from tokens is directly interpolated into SQL strings without parameterized queries or escaping. Line 59 uses .format() to insert self.tokens.word directly into an ILIKE query. Lines 62, 66, 67, 70 also directly interpolate user input. An attacker can inject SQL via the 'q' parameter by crafting a search query that produces malicious tokens.

MongoDB query construction uses .format() to interpolate user-controlled tokens directly into query strings. Lines 56, 59, 62, 65 construct MongoDB queries with unescaped user input from tokens.field, tokens.word, tokens.string, and tokens.regex. These are then passed through json.loads(repr(...)) which doesn't prevent injection.

findings.suggested_fix: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements. For PostgreSQL, use psycopg2 parameterized queries with %s placeholders and pass parameters separately. For MongoDB, ensure all user input is properly validated and use MongoDB's query operators safely without string interpolation. Escape special characters in regex patterns and validate field names against a whitelist.

findings.explanation: MongoDB query construction uses .format() to interpolate user-controlled tokens directly into query strings. Lines 56, 59, 62, 65 construct MongoDB queries with unescaped user input from tokens.field, tokens.word, tokens.string, and tokens.regex. These are then passed through json.loads(repr(...)) which doesn't prevent injection.
findings.suggested_fix: Build MongoDB query objects programmatically using Python dictionaries instead of string formatting. For example: `{self.tokens.field: {"$regex": self.tokens.word}}` should be constructed as `{self.tokens.field: {"$regex": mongo_escape(self.tokens.word)}}` or use a library that safely constructs BSON queries. Implement input validation and field name whitelisting.

findings.explanation: The code checks `if g.get('customers', None)` and applies a customer_query filter. This appears to enforce customer-based access control. The authorization check is present and customer filtering is applied to queries when customers are set in the Flask g object.
